title: Review of c23's CIPS metabolic claim (SIE): on fresh seed 5 ~300 enzyme droplets condense from noise and 209 persist to t=2000 in the fed run; stopping fuel regrowth at t=1500 dissolves all of them by t~1600 while total enzyme stays exactly constant
summary: Ran world.py unchanged on fresh seed 5 (256^2, t=2000, labkit), fed and with fork_t=1500 (kF -> 0 everywhere). Fed: from uniform enzyme plus noise, droplets appear at t~170-270 (297 at most), coarsen by merges (84) to 209 by t=2000, 229 persistent tracks, 0 splits; enzyme total drift 0.0. Fork (identical until t=1500): the fuel total drops to 0 within ~20 t and the droplet count falls from ~225 to 0 by t~1600 (rerun/fork/timeseries.png), while the enzyme total stays at 1.0 of its initial value: the droplets dissolve back into a uniform enzyme field rather than being destroyed.

observations.S: rerun/fed/sheet.png t=0-80: uniform field; droplets by t=270
observations.I: rerun/fed/sheet.png: ~200-300 discrete droplets of bounded size persisting to t=2000 (229 persistent tracks)
observations.E: rerun/fork/timeseries.png: fuel exhausted at t~1520, components ~225 -> 0 by t~1600, enzyme total flat; fed twin keeps 209

controls_run.E: rerun/fork (fork_t=1500) vs rerun/fed, identical until t=1500

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; I did not repeat the local feed cuts. The droplets coarsen by merges with no size cap and never divide, as the author states; 'dies' here means dissolution of a condensate into a uniform field when its fuel stops.
